Polmonite da COVID-19: opacità a vetro s: COVID-19 pneumonia: bilateral peripheral ground-glass opacities (typical pattern)
Uomo di 70 anni, pregressa sternotomia,: 70-year-old man, prior sternotomy, fever and dyspnea. On the same day bedside AP chest X-ray and contrast-enhanced chest CT (performed as CT angiography to exclude embolism).
Report in order: X-ray, CT, conclusion.
Nella polmonite da COVID-19 la TC mostra:
In COVID-19 pneumonia CT typically shows bilateral, peripheral and posterior, multilobar ground-glass opacities, sometimes with a "crazy paving" appearance or with consolidations in later phases. The RSNA consensus (2020) classifies the picture as typical, indeterminate, atypical or negative: the bilateral peripheral pattern is "typical".
Bedside X-ray is poorly sensitive in the early phases: the opacities are faint and peripheral, often basal. The diagnosis remains virologic (swab).
Differential diagnosis of bilateral ground glass: other viral pneumonias, organizing pneumonia, edema (usually central and with effusions, septal thickening and cardiomegaly), hemorrhage, drug-induced pneumonitis.
Vetro smerigliato bilaterale periferico: Bilateral peripheral and posterior ground glass: typical pattern of COVID-19, but the diagnosis is made by the swab.
Tampone positivo per SARS-CoV-2 (dati cl: Swab positive for SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19-AR clinical data). Original CT report: "Diffuse, peripheral patchy ground-glass opacities are seen throughout the lungs". No intensive care admission.
Polmonite da COVID-19 in un paziente già: COVID-19 pneumonia in an already hospitalized patient with fever and dyspnea: the picture is the one being sought and is communicated with the report; the physician is notified by voice only if unexpected complications appear (pneumothorax, embolism).
